title: Moved to tears by playing New Orleans music
summary: Overwhelmed by yesterday's performance and the richness of his life in music.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Right. Hey what are you doing here? You get in the truck too. You never know. But New Orleans has been great for me personally. My life and my life experiences, like a tear up and I well up when I think about it, like yesterday performing, I was telling my wife, you know, I always forget to bring a handkerchief. Because, you know, when the spirit, with the musicians that I played with yesterday, it’s overwhelming for me, and I’m sure a lot of times for a lot of musicians. It’s such a spiritual thing, or, I don’t know, that’s the best way to describe it. But it’s a very moving thing. And what happens with me is, first the music is moving, and then it all starts going to me like why it’s even happening, like because I made the decision to move to New Orleans, because I played all these years with Leroy Jones and because, you know, then you start thinking about the things like with Sandy of course, that brought all the memories of Katrina back. And all of these things, oh I’ve traveled the world, and how can I have a life like this? I haven’t made a lot of money but man, my life is so rich. I mean, you know, it’s overwhelming for me. So I start crying. I was crying yesterday. That was like, I don’t know I was trying to figure out if I was going to be able to sing. Because my nose was running. I didn’t have a handkerchief, I always forget. Because it’s really great. It’s really been great. And then you know, to come here, and have all of these friends meet you, as a result of, just cause I can play music? You know? New Orleans music? It’s something special. It’s really special. And I can feel it and I can say it, but I can’t make anybody else feel it. I know what I feel.
